action: Review browser extensions installed in developer mode, especially utilities asking for broad permissions. Audit webmail and case-management pages for script tags loading from unfamiliar domains, and investigate OneDrive activity to tenants outside your organisation.
exec: Browser-based spying leaves few traces on disk, so endpoint tools can miss it; webmail portals and browser extensions need checking.
plain: Researchers found spies running hidden code inside the web browsers of government workers in the Middle East and Southeast Asia, stealing logins and reading email without leaving files on the computer.

key_findings: Targets were defence, interior and foreign ministries, a telecom provider and government email in the Middle East, plus police, justice, military and foreign affairs bodies in Southeast Asia.
Falcon C2 runs JavaScript in the victim's browser over encrypted WebSockets to steal passwords, cookies and email and to proxy through logged-in sessions.
Entry methods were script tags injected into a ministry's Roundcube webmail (39 instances affected), a fake Flash update and a sideloaded 'PDF Viewer' extension requesting 40 permissions.
A Rust implant named Antino uses Microsoft OneDrive as its command channel.
Unit 42 assesses with high confidence that Falcon and the earlier PeckBirdy framework are variants of one core; it names no actor.
recommendations: Review extensions installed in developer mode that pose as utilities and request permissions such as all URLs, debugger or native messaging.
Audit webmail, ticketing and case-management pages for script tags loading from unfamiliar external domains.
Look for web-analytics style cookies or storage keys on internal apps where analytics has no reason to appear.
Investigate OAuth activity to OneDrive tenants outside your organisation, especially repeated small JSON writes.

summary: Unit 42 reports that a framework called Falcon C2 ran malicious JavaScript inside the browsers of government staff in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries between March and May 2026. It steals passwords, cookies and email, and lets attackers browse as the victim. Delivery included injected scripts on a foreign ministry's Roundcube webmail and a fake PDF viewer extension. No actor is named.
title: Unit 42: Falcon C2 turns victims' browsers into spying tools at Middle East and Asian ministries

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 report.
